author: Times News
description:
As the war in Iran drags beyond Donald Trump’s predicted "quick victory", the friction in Washington is moving from the battlefield to the bank balance. While the President oscillates between threats of total destruction and claims of "fruitful negotiations", billions are being moved on financial markets by those seemingly one step ahead of his tweets. This episode unpicks the strategic stalemate where Iranian regime survival counts as a win, and explores how domestic chaos—from $5 gasoline to grounded flights—is curdling the MAGA message from within.

00:00 The 48-hour bluff and Trump’s negotiation claims
03:10 Why Iranian survival counts as a victory
05:07 Insider trading and the "Banana Republic" shift
09:12 The Iranian regime’s JD Vance "trolling"
15:35 The escalation trap: deployment vs. land war
22:45 Domestic fallout: $5 gasoline and airport chaos
27:10 Mar-a-Lago turns blue: a symbolic Republican defeat

description:
Today we go inside Operation Titan, as North Yorkshire Police fight back against county lines drugs gangs. But with each line the police shut down, another pops up in its place, sometimes within days. The Sunday Times' northern editor David Collins investigates how to break the cycle. 

This is episode two of a five-part special investigation into county lines drug dealing, running in audio, video, print and digital from The Times and The Sunday Times.
